title: Make the brief CLI deadline test independent of host load
body:
Outcome: test/rules/brief-allowlist.test.ts:102 ('brief CLI handles maximum-sized section lines before its one-second deadline') does not fail under host load. It spawns the brief CLI with a 1000 ms wall-clock timeout (line 114); on 2026-11-05 at load average 37 it failed once in node scripts/test-suite.mjs test/slice/slice-run.test.ts test/rules and passed twice in isolation (t-xgwxm6z pre-commit run). A wall-clock bound on a spawned process measures host load, not the parser's complexity.
Proof: the test asserts a load-independent bound (for example an operation count or a linear-time property on the parser in-process) and stays green under parallel load; no retry policy (D12).
